abstract: We investigate fundamental limits on broadband electromagnetic absorption by a material-coated perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) sphere. Exact reflection coefficients are derived for the transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) spherical modes. Their long-wavelength asymptotics, combined with causality and contour integration in the complex wavelength plane, yield sum rules relating the wavelength-integrated modal reflection to the static material parameters, coating thickness, curvature, and complex reflection zeros. For the dipolar modes ($n=1$), known passive spherical-wave sum rules establish analytically a material-dependent lower bound on the weighted logarithmic reflection integral. Extension to higher-order modes requires a nonnegativity condition on higher odd moments of the reflection zeros; we formulate this condition as a conjecture and provide extensive Monte-Carlo evidence for passive dispersive coatings. The resulting bounds establish a per-channel absorption--bandwidth tradeoff and reveal the spherical-harmonic order as a discrete transverse-wavenumber variable, recovering the familiar planar attenuation factor in the locally planar limit. Finally, we show how the modal bounds can be combined for a localized external source. For a radial electric dipole outside the sphere, the near-field excitation is decomposed into TM spherical channels, leading to a source-weighted broadband absorption bound. As the source approaches the surface, progressively higher angular momenta contribute, directly linking near-field spatial localization to the hierarchy of modal absorption constraints.
